anchor: Cloud computing as digital infrastructure: scalable, network-delivered access to computing resources
argumentsAgainst: Cloud expansion can increase exposure to cyber threats, vendor dependence and concentration of sensitive data; these are analytical risks, not claims made in the supplied official summary.
Energy, land and water demands of data centres may create sustainability pressures; the supplied official summary does not establish these impacts.
argumentsFor: Cloud infrastructure can support scalable and cost-effective access to storage, servers, software and data processing.
A national cloud ecosystem can strengthen digital governance and public-service delivery while supporting control over sensitive data.
Cloud capacity can support governance, business, finance and emerging AI applications.
background: Cloud computing provides computing services such as storage, servers, software and data processing over the internet.

indiaImplications: A stronger cloud ecosystem can improve the scalability and responsiveness of e-governance platforms.
Public-sector cloud adoption requires attention to cybersecurity, data governance, interoperability and continuity of services.
Domestic cloud capability can contribute to technological autonomy, but policy should avoid excessive dependence on a small number of providers.

sections.heading: Cloud as a governance layer
paragraphs: The Press Information Bureau record is titled “Cloud Ecosystem in India” and is dated 29 October 2026. The retrieved PIB material describes cloud as internet-delivered access to storage, servers, software and data processing. Its mechanism is pooled, on-demand computing capacity rather than exclusively fixed local infrastructure.

This can make digital services more adaptable when demand changes and can support governance, business and finance. The limitation is that cloud adoption alone does not guarantee privacy, cybersecurity or strategic autonomy; those outcomes depend on architecture, contracts, standards and oversight.

sections.heading: Sovereignty and safeguards
paragraphs: The retrieved PIB material connects India’s cloud infrastructure with data sovereignty, digital governance and public-service delivery, and describes MeghRaj as the government’s national cloud platform. This indicates a policy emphasis on retaining control while using scalable digital resources.

For examination analysis, the central trade-off is between efficiency and control. India would need interoperable systems, strong security practices, transparent procurement, resilient backup arrangements and accountable handling of sensitive data. These are analytical recommendations, not claims contained in the supplied official summary.
